newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. Bruno softens stand on rent controls - paper.
newsitem.headline: N.Y. Bruno softens stand on rent controls - paper.

text.p: New York State Senate Majority Leader Joseph Bruno (R-Troy) softened his stand on ending rent controls saying he would support keeping protections for poor renters, the New York Times said on Tuesday.
The Republican senator earlier had called for eliminating most rent regulations by mid-1999, adding elderly and disabled renters would be protected.
Under Bruno's plan, rent regulations, which cover about 1.2 million apartments in New York City, would end for any unit that became vacant after June 15, 1997.

The battle over the rent regulations is expected to become a key factor in the fight over the state's budget for fiscal year 1998. Gov George Pataki, a critic of rent regulations, has said Bruno's plan would end them too quickly, the paper said. It quoted Assembly Speaker, Sheldon Silver (D-Manhattan), who is expected to lead the fight for tenant groups, as saying Bruno's softer stand was a step in the right direction.
New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani has said he does not see any need to weaken rent protections now, the paper said.
